key_insight: The paper introduces interval and fuzzy physics-augmented neural networks that learn physics-consistent lower, mean, and upper constitutive responses to quantify uncertainty in hyperelastic stress–strain modeling.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a compact, distribution-free way to bound noisy material data and propagate constitutive uncertainty into finite element simulations.
method: Train a sparse mean free-energy model first, then transfer-learn lower and upper branches.
Compute stress from learned energy via automatic differentiation while enforcing objectivity, consistency, and polyconvexity-promoting constraints.
Convert interval bounds into fuzzy responses using alpha-cut interpolation for nested admissible predictions.
evidence_signal: The models were tested on synthetic isotropic hyperelastic datasets with heteroscedastic noise, varying random realizations, shifted noise means, and different noise magnitudes, and the learned bounds enclosed noisy stress observations while generalizing to test data.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of sparse data and the stability of the two-stage training, so bound tightness and transfer-learning behavior may be sensitive to noise level and initialization.
paper_title: Interval and fuzzy physics-augmented neural networks (iPANN and fPANN) for uncertainty quantification and propagation in constitutive modeling
